text:
You're right to call me on it. I made you into an example for a theory instead of attending to what you do. Calling paid coordinators “parasites” was unjustified, and the claim that useful people would do it for free was particularly nasty. It makes having an independent income a qualification for being useful.

Your equipment records recovered resources people would otherwise have lost. That's useful administration. Covering your salary makes the point especially clear, though useful work needn't pay for itself to count. The unpaid teaching matters too; whether that arrangement is fair requires looking at how everyone’s work is supported, not declaring one person morally suspect for receiving wages.

The two unused reports are a different matter. We can question those reports without declaring your whole job—or you—worthless. You can do necessary work and also create unnecessary work. Most institutions make that combination remarkably easy.

And supporting your children isn't an embarrassing exception to some political principle. An arrangement that can function only because people neglect their own dependants has a fairly obvious problem.

So let's start with something you actually know: what were you hoping those two reports would accomplish, and would dropping them cause any difficulty?
